title: Power Automate process mining: export object-centric models to a Microsoft Fabric semantic model
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, optional export workflow, licensing and governance claims are supported. The billing description should add Azure's one-minute minimum to its statement about per-second Fabric capacity billing.

claims.claim: The roadmap identifies Power Automate as the product.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Automate"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is August CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "August CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is May CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "May CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: General Availability is a listed release phase.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: Preview is also a listed release phase.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists no government clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap says the capability is enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: Power Automate Process Mining can publish an object-centric process model to a Fabric workspace.
claims.quote: In the Choose where to export step, select Continue to set up the export of OCPM semantic model in your Fabric workspace, or Skip export.

claims.claim: Publishing creates a new Direct Lake semantic model.
claims.quote: When you publish a process to Fabric workspace, it creates a new DirectLake semantic model and an empty Power BI report connected to the semantic model.

claims.claim: Publishing creates an empty Power BI report connected to the semantic model.
claims.quote: When you publish a process to Fabric workspace, it creates a new DirectLake semantic model and an empty Power BI report connected to the semantic model.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The exported semantic model is built on Fabric Lakehouse delta tables.
claims.quote: The semantic model is created on top of Fabric Lakehouse delta tables.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Choose where to export is optional, offering Continue or Skip export.
claims.quote: In the Choose where to export step, select Continue to set up the export of OCPM semantic model in your Fabric workspace, or Skip export.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The maker selects the destination from available Fabric workspaces.
claims.quote: Select from the list of available Fabric workspaces.

claims.claim: The maker selects a Fabric Lakehouse in the destination workspace.
claims.quote: Select a Fabric Lakehouse in the workspace.

claims.claim: The maker selects the name of the default report.
claims.quote: Select a name for the default report that will be created for the resulting semantic model.

claims.claim: The semantic model contains object types.
claims.quote: Object Types | List of all types of objects in the process.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The semantic model contains objects and ingested object-level attributes.
claims.quote: Objects | List of all objects in the process with reference to object type, lifecycle of the object, and relevant object level attributes as additional columns (when ingested).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The semantic model contains events and ingested event-level attributes.
claims.quote: Events | Entity holds list of all events in the process with reference to particular node in the Nodes table and ingested event level attributes as additional columns.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The model preserves relationships between events and objects.
claims.quote: EventObjectRelations | Entity holds all relationships between Events and Objects “touched” by the execution of an event.

claims.claim: The model includes derived nodes and edges used for visualisation.
claims.quote: They include items derived from the raw data by process mining algorithms and usually serve visualization purposes.

claims.claim: The model includes process executions identified using a leading object type.
claims.quote: Process execution data entities are calculated as process instances of interconnected objects based on a leading object type.

claims.claim: The published data model has predefined relationships.
claims.quote: The published data model includes predefined relationships that handle filtering and interconnectivity of visuals.

claims.claim: Some relationships are hidden because only one relationship between the same two tables can be active.
claims.quote: Some relationships are hidden in the model. This limitation exists because only one relationship between the same two tables can be active in semantic models.

claims.claim: The allowed Lakehouse column-name characters are English letters, digits and underscores.
claims.quote: Allowed characters include: a-z: lowercase English letters; A-Z: uppercase English letters; 0-9: digits; _: underscore

claims.claim: Other Lakehouse column-name characters are replaced with underscores.
claims.quote: All other characters are replaced with an underscore (_) as part of the sanitization process.

claims.claim: Semantic-model columns use the original column names rather than the sanitised Lakehouse names.
claims.quote: Lakehouse delta table columns therefore use the sanitized column names, whereas semantic model columns use the original column names.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Export can be interrupted when sanitisation gives two columns the same name, such as Customer_Name and Customer Name.
claims.quote: This process might result in rare situations where export isn't successful, as the ingested data source includes two columns that result in identical names after sanitization—Customer_Name and Customer Name.

claims.claim: A column-name collision causes an error notification to the user.
claims.quote: The export is interrupted and user is notified with the specific error message.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Power Automate Process Mining automatically keeps the semantic model up to date by default.
claims.quote: By default, Power Automate Process Mining automatically keeps the semantic model up to date.

claims.claim: The semantic model Settings screen has a Keep your Direct Lake data up to date flag that can be turned off.
claims.quote: you might want to remove the potential intermediate inconsistencies by turning off the Keep your Direct Lake data up to date flag in the Settings screen of the semantic model.

claims.claim: Updating that screen requires taking ownership with Take over at the top of Settings first.
claims.quote: Before you update this screen, you need to take ownership of the semantic model by selecting Take over at the top of the Settings screen.

claims.claim: Learn documents a Power BI composite model on top of the published model for additional data sources.
claims.quote: Use the Power BI composite model on top of the semantic model published by Power Automate Process Mining and create the necessary modifications for these scenarios: You need to create more data sources.

claims.claim: The model's Direct Lake access-mode option is Automatic.
claims.quote: The semantic model uses DirectLake access mode, but its option is set to Automatic.

claims.claim: Nonoptimal DAX or an incorrectly configured composite model can cause fallback to DirectQuery.
claims.quote: using nonoptimal DAX queries or incorrectly setting a composite model might result in fallback to DirectQuery mode.

claims.claim: DirectQuery fallback may lower report performance.
claims.quote: This setting means that your report doesn't break, but you might experience lower performance.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes configurable publishing schedules.
claims.quote: Data refresh synchronization: Configure publishing schedules to keep Fabric semantic models current with your process mining data updates.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes preserving KPIs as semantic-model measures.
claims.quote: Metric preservation: Transfer KPIs and metrics from your process analysis, making them available as measures within the Fabric semantic model.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes combining process intelligence with other Fabric data sources.
claims.quote: Enterprise connectivity: Combine process intelligence data with other Fabric data sources, enabling unified analytics across operational, financial, and customer domains.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the published models follow Fabric architecture and are compatible with existing governance.
claims.quote: The published semantic models follow Fabric's standard architecture, ensuring compatibility with existing governance policies, security controls, and data management practices within your Microsoft environment.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The ingest page labels its link to the export documentation as preview.
claims.quote: Learn more in Export OCPM semantic model into Fabric workspace (preview).

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The ingest workflow lets makers map financial event-level and object-level attributes.
claims.quote: Event and Object level attributes (including financial) are optional but highly recommended for more detailed analysis

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Workspace roles implicitly grant permissions on the published semantic model.
claims.quote: A user's role in a workspace implicitly grants them permissions on the semantic models in the workspace, as described in the following table.

claims.claim: The OCPM pages do not specify additional explicit permission grants made by the export.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "semantic model" "explicit" "permissions"; opened OCPM ingest and semantic-model pages and Semantic model permissions. General grants are documented, but no export-specific explicit grants are stated.

claims.claim: The OCPM pages do not specify default report sharing by the export.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "semantic model" export licensing meter permissions sharing schedule; opened OCPM ingest and semantic-model pages and Semantic model permissions. The export creates an empty report; default sharing is not stated.

claims.claim: The ingest guide instructs makers to store the event log as CSV in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.
claims.quote: Then, store the resulting file in a CSV format in either Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.

claims.claim: The event-log creation guide additionally lists a Fabric Lakehouse delta table as an ingestion source.
claims.quote: The current version supports data ingestion from a CSV file stored in Azure Data Lake or OneLake or delta table stored in the Fabric Lakehouse.

claims.claim: Refresh Data triggers full ingestion and creation of the process model.
claims.quote: Refresh Data: Button to reload and refresh the displayed analytics with the most recent data (this action triggers the full ingestion and creation of the process model).

claims.claim: The custom-workspace report page requires the OneLake external-app access option to be switched on.
claims.quote: Ensure that Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to the Fabric option is switched on in the OneLake tenant settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls: prose
claims.claim: The custom-workspace report page requires Process Insights Prod to have workspace admin access.
claims.quote: Select Search for, and then add Process Insights Prod. Assign it admin access. It's a requirement that the service principal gets added as an admin. If you skip this step, the feature doesn't work.

claims.claim: The custom-workspace page requires at least Contributor access for the maker using an existing workspace.
claims.quote: You can also use an already existing Fabric workspace. Ensure that your account has at least Contributor access rights in that workspace and ensure you meet the other prerequisites.

claims.claim: The custom-workspace report page warns that reusing a report name overwrites another process's report.
claims.quote: If you use a report name that already exists, the process mining capability overwrites the existing report of another process.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Open questions
claims.claim: The OCPM pages do not confirm whether the custom-workspace OneLake and service-principal prerequisites govern the export step.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "Process Insights" "OneLake" prerequisites; opened OCPM ingest, export and custom-workspace pages. The OneLake ingestion prerequisite result concerns the input connection, not the optional export destination.

claims.claim: Process mining is licensed as part of Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium is a per-user licence providing process-mining capabilities.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license with the following offerings:

claims.claim: Each Power Automate Premium licence adds 50 MB of process-mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: Premium's contributed process-mining capacity is pooled tenant-wide up to 100 GB.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Beyond that 100 GB pool, the Process Mining add-on is needed to process more data.
claims.quote: When you reach 100 GB, you need to purchase the Power Automate Process Mining add-on to process more data.

claims.claim: The FAQ lists the Process Mining add-on at $5,000 USD for 100 GB of data stored per month.
claims.quote: List Price (USD): $5,000 for 100 GB of data stored/month

claims.claim: Power Automate Premium is the prerequisite for the Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: Required prerequisite: Power Automate Premium. Multiple add-ons can be applied to a single prerequisite.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power BI licences are not included in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: Power BI licenses aren't included in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.claim: The process-mining overview names a Power BI Premium licence for report customisation.
claims.quote: To customize your report, you need to link the process to your own Power BI workspace, and a Power BI Premium license.

claims.claim: The FAQ instead lists Power BI Pro, Power BI per user or Power BI Premium capacity for further customisation and analysis.
claims.quote: In order to customize and analyze your process mining results further, you might want to acquire more Power BI Pro*, Power BI per user, or Power BI premium capacity licenses if you haven't already done so.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Fabric and Power BI platform licensing applies to the export's Lakehouse, semantic model and report.
claims.quote: Power BI items include: Reports; Semantic models. Non-Power BI Fabric items include everything else, such as: Lakehouses

claims.claim: Fabric supports F capacities, trial capacities and eligible P capacities with Fabric enabled.
claims.quote: Fabric (F SKUs) ... All Fabric experiences; Fabric Trial ... All Fabric experiences; Power BI Premium per capacity (P1–P5) only ... Yes (Fabric items disabled until enabled by Fabric Admin)

claims.claim: F capacities are purchased through Azure and billed per second.
claims.quote: You purchase F capacities through Azure, and Azure bills you per second with no commitment ... Pricing is regional, and Azure bills per second with a one-minute minimum.
claims.fix: Add 'with a one-minute minimum' after 'per second' in Cost and licensing and the cost rationale, as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/enterprise/licenses.

claims.claim: The Azure pay-as-you-go F capacity option has no commitment.
claims.quote: You can use an Azure capacity for as long as you want without commitment.

claims.claim: Azure offers a yearly Fabric capacity reservation.
claims.quote: with the option of a yearly capacity reservation to save costs.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Creating Power BI items outside My workspace and sharing them requires Pro, PPU or a Power BI individual trial.
claims.quote: To create Power BI items in a workspace other than My workspace and share them, you need a Power BI Pro or a Power BI Premium Per-User (PPU) license, or a Power BI individual trial.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The OCPM pages name no separate export-specific licence or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "export" "licensing" "meter"; opened OCPM ingest and export, process-mining overview, Power Platform licensing FAQ and Fabric licenses. Platform licensing is documented; no separate OCPM export licence or meter is named.

claims.claim: Environment Maker is required to create, share and contribute to processes.
claims.quote: You need the Environment Maker role to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.claim: Process mining requires a Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Power Platform environment with a Microsoft Dataverse database.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The maker path is Process mining > Start here > Object-centric process mining > Process name > Data source > Azure Data Lake or OneLake > Continue > Choose where to export > Continue or Skip export.
claims.quote: Under the Data source heading, select Azure Data Lake or OneLake and select Continue. ... In the Choose where to export step, select Continue to set up the export of OCPM semantic model in your Fabric workspace, or Skip export.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: No API for the maker's OCPM export choice is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "export" "API" "Dataverse"; Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell Dataverse object-centric process mining export Fabric workspace. Read ingest/export and PAC/admin programmability excerpts; no export API documented.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The OneLake external-app access setting is at OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings > Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to Fabric.
claims.quote: OneLake tenant settings are configured in Configurations > Tenant settings in the Govern section of the OneLake catalog. ... Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to Fabric

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row and prose
claims.claim: GET https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/admin/tenantsettings lists tenant settings rather than changing them.
claims.quote: Returns a list of the tenant settings. ... GET https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/admin/tenantsettings

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The List Tenant Settings caller must be a Fabric administrator or authenticate with a service principal.
claims.quote: The caller must be a Fabric administrator or authenticate using a service principal.

claims.claim: Power Platform administrators and Fabric administrators have control over organisation-wide Fabric settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform administrator or Fabric administrator ... These roles provide access to the admin experience in Govern and control over organization-wide Fabric settings, usage metrics, and admin features, except for licensing.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no administrator setting specifically for the OCPM export step at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "export" "administrator" "setting"; "object-centric" "export" "admin" Power Automate setting API Power Platform Dataverse. Opened OCPM ingest/export and OneLake settings; none gives an export-specific admin switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The export is user-opt-in: each maker chooses it or skips it, and nothing is exported until that choice.
claims.quote: In the Choose where to export step, select Continue to set up the export of OCPM semantic model in your Fabric workspace, or Skip export.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining per-user process-mining licensing, capacity add-ons and Fabric platform licensing.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license ... The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.claim: Variable is an appropriate cost classification because the export uses Fabric capacity with Azure-metered F capacity options.
claims.quote: Azure (F capacities): You purchase F capacities through Azure, and Azure bills you per second with no commitment, with the option of a yearly capacity reservation to save costs.

claims.claim: The sources do not say existing processes are exported automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "export" "administrator" "setting". Read roadmap, ingest and export pages: automatic availability and model refresh are described, but automatic export of existing processes is not.

claims.claim: The OCPM Learn pages describe automatic model refresh but do not describe an OCPM publishing-schedule setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "publishing" "schedule"; "object-centric" "semantic model" export licensing meter permissions sharing schedule. Opened ingest, semantic-model and process-overview pages; no OCPM publishing-schedule setting is described.
